Petitioner has filed this petition U/sec.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming the compensation
amount of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.

Petitioner case is as Follows:

That on 12.11.2023 at about 10.20 AM., she was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg No.KA-01-JT-6402 near PAR Kalyana Mantapa, Malur - Hosur road, Malur taluk,
wherein the driver of the Car bearing Reg No.KA- 19-ME-4110 drove it, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the two wheeler and caused the accident, in the accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

She was shifted to Gourav hospital,
wherein she took treatment as inpatient for the accidental injuries and she has spent Rs.3,00,000/- for her treatment.
3. Petitioner stated that she is 32 years of age and she is working as a Teacher and she was earning Rs.35,000/- per month,

Further she stated that the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle and the jurisdictional police have registered Cr.No.457/2023 against the driver of the offending vehicle.

Petitioner alleged that the Respondent no.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and he insured his vehicle with respondent no.1 and accident caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and as such both are liable to pay the compensation with interest and he prayer this tribunal to award the compensation amount by allowing the petition.
4. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, respondent No.2 has not chosen to contest the petition and he placed exparte.
Respondent No.1 appeared through their counsel filed power and written statement by denying the entire version of the petition in toto.
Respondent No.1 contended that insured has violated the policy conditions and the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner and they prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.
5. Petitioner examined herself as PW-1 and examined the orthopedic surgeon as PW.2, produced and marked 20 documents which are at Ex.P.1 to 20 and they are fully cross examined.
6. Respondent No.1 examined the official of foundation school as RW-1 produced and marked 3 documents which are Ex.D1 to 3.
Cross examination of RW-1 is taken as nil as prayed for.
7. I have heard the arguments from the counsels appearing for both the sides.
I have perused the same along with entire records.

8. On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following :
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 12.11.2023 at about 10.20 AM., she was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg No.KA- Lakshmamma R vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101181443/
2 01-JT-6402 near PAR Kalyana Mantapa, Malur - Hosur road, Malur taluk, wherein the driver of the Car bearing Reg No.KA-19- ME-4110 drove it, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the two wheeler and caused the accident, in the accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries as alleged in the petition ?

2. Whether respondent No.1 proves that insured has violated the policy conditions and accident occurred due to the negligence act of the petitioner and vehicle belongs to respondent No.2 is not involved in the accident as contended in the written statement?.
3 Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?

if so, what is the quantum and from whom?
4.What order or award?
9.

After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
Issue no.1: In the affirmative Issue no.2: In the negative Issue no.3: In partly affirmative Issue no.4:
As per final order for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 to 3 :- I have taken these issues together for common discussion so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW.1 being the petitioner, she reiterated the petition averments in her examination-in-chief affidavit.

Petitioner has tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, complaint, mahazar, sketch,
IMV report and final report, which are at Ex.P.1 to 5 & 8.
11.
On careful perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents, It is evident that one Sri.Shivakumar S/o Sadashivaiah was the driver of the offending vehicle as on the date of the accident.

Mahazar,
sketch, IMV report, final report establishes the involvement of the offending vehicle and the negligent act of the driver in the alleged accident.

Further ExP.7 is the reply notice given by respondent No.2 wherein he admit that Sri.Shivakumar was the driver of his vehicle and he was having valid driving license and insurance policy of the said vehicle was valid as on the date of the accident.
12. In the cross-examination of PW-1, nothing worth is elicited to disprove the allegation.
The alleged negligent act of the petitioner is not suggested to PW-1.
Respondent No.1 has failed to establish its contention that accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner and respondent No.2 has violated the policy conditions.

13. The final report which is at Ex.P8 is filed after investigation and it is the prima facie proof of the accident and the involvement of the offending vehicle and rash and negligent act of the driver of the Lakshmamma R vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101181443/
3 offending vehicle.

sentences.text: Accordingly the police records cannot be doubted and disbelieved as it has reached the finality.

14. Petitioner has tender the discharge summaries as per Ex.P10, 14 & 15, the entry therein reveals that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries that is Left femur fracture and patella fracture and CRIF with nailing was done to left femur and tension bind wiring for patella on 15.11.2023 and she has taken treatment for accidental injuries as inpatient for 4 days in the hospital and petitioner has spent Rs.1,55,566/- for her medical expenses as per Ex.P.11 & 16.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following heads.

15. Pecuniary damages (Medical expenses) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization,
Medicines, Transportation, Nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure:
16.
Petitioner took treatment at Gaurav hospital.
Evidently nothing is elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disbelieve the fact that she has sustained the grievous injuries in the alleged accident and she took treatment for the same.
Inasmuch, discharge summaries and the medical reports issued form the hospital has to be accepted.
Admittedly petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient for 4 days.
Further for the attendant charges, transportation, nourishing food, she might have spend some more expenses.

Therefore I award Rs.10,000/-, in total petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,65,566/-
under this head.
Loss of income during laid up period.

17. The petitioner has tendered salary certificates, bank statement as per Ex.P.12 and 13. RW-1 being the official of Foundation school, deposed that petitioner was working in their school till the date of accident and she is not working till this date in their school.
As per the pay slips the Salary of the petitioner for the month of November 2023 is Rs.20,800/- and she is not income tax assessee.
Accordingly her monthly income has to be assessed by deducting the professional tax and it is Rs.20,600/-.
Considering the accidental injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, I am of view that, she has lost her income for fifteen days.
Therefore I award Rs.10,300/- as compensation under this head.
Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
18. The petitioner has examined the Orthopedic surgeon Sri.B.N.Nagaraj as PW-2.

He deposed on the basis wound certificate and discharge summary, and clinical examination of the petition that,
petitioner has 16% of whole body disability as per Ex.P19 & 20, and petitioner required another surgery for removal implants.
I have perused the evidence of PW-2 wound certificate, discharge summaries given by the hospital, X-ray etc.
Evidently petitioner has not examined the doctor who has treated her in the hospital.
Petitioner sustained grievous injuries that is Left femur fracture and patella fracture and CRIF with nailing was done to left femur and tension bind wiring for patella on 15.11.2023.

Further in the cross examination of PW-2, he deposed that fracture is not united and implants are yet to be removed and petitioner can do her routine work with difficulty and there is no loss of muscle power for her.
The oral testimony of PW-2 corroborates with Ex.P.19 & 20.

sentences.text: Admittedly petitioner has no functional disability.
Petitioner has not tendered resignation letter nor the documents show that she cannot do teaching in sitting position.
The physical disability of the petitioner will not affect for her profession of teaching in sitting position.
The percentage of loss of earning capacity due to accidental injuries is different from the percentage of physical disability due to accidental injuries.
Considering the medical reports and oral testimony of doctor, the whole body disability of the petitioner is assessed as 8%.

The notional monthly income of the petitioner is assessed as Rs.20,600/-, the age of petitioner as on the date of accident is 36 years and 7 months and 2 days as per the entry in Aadhar card, which are at ExP.9.
The multiplier applicable to this case is "15".

Therefore loss of income on account of permanent disability is calculated as follows;
Rs.20,600/-(Monthly income) X 12 (Months) X 15 ( Multiplier) X8% (Disability) = Rs.2,96,640/-
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.2,96,640/- as compensation under this head.
Non-Pecuniary damages (General damages) (IV)Damages for pain and sufferings and loss of amenities:
19.
It is undisputed fact that petitioner has sustained grievous injury.
During the hospitalization and rehabilitation period, she might have undergone lot of pain and sufferings and due to accidental injuries.
Therefore I award Rs.20,000/- under these conventional heads.

V) Loss of Amenities :-
20.
The petitioner has to forego certain amenities available for her.

Therefore I award Rs.10,000/-
as compensation under this head.
As per the oral testimony of PW-2, another surgery is required for the petitioner, for the removal of implants.
The estimated cost of the surgery is not tendered.
Tentatively petitioner is entitled for Rs.25,000/- for the additional surgery.
21. Except these heads the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under any other heads.
In all the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:

Sl No Particulars Amount  1 Towards medicines, attendant charges, Rs.1,65,566/-
 transportation, nourishing food  2 Loss of income during the laid up period Rs. 10,300/-
 3 Loss of income on account of Rs.2,96,640/-
 permanent physical disability  4 pain & sufferings Rs. 20,000/-
 5 loss of amenities Rs. 10,000/-
 6 Cost of additional surgery Rs. 25,000/-

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

sentences.text: Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
23. Liability:

The insurance company has not disputed the validity of the policy issued to the offending vehicle, on the other hand, they have failed to established its defence that accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner and insured has violated the policy conditions.

As such respondent No.1 is the liable to pay the compensation amount with interest, respondent No.1 is directed to deposit compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of this order.

Hence with the aforesaid discussion based on the evidence placed on record,
Accordingly I am answering Issue No.1 the affirmative, Issue No.2 in negative & issue No.3 in partly affirmative.
24. Issue No.4:
For the foregoing reason and discussion, on the aforesaid issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor vehicle Act,1988, is partly allowed with cost.
Petitioner is entitled for the compensation amount of Rs.5,27,506/-with interest at the rate of 6% P.A from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
Respondent no.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this tribunal with in 30 days from the date of the judgment.

After depositing the compensation amount with interest, Cash sheristedar is directed to release the entire amount to the petitioner through K2, after compliance of mandate of circular No.39/2020 dated 17.01.2020.
Advocate fee of Rs.1000/- is fixed.
All the interim applications pending if any stands disposed of.
Draw award accordingly.
